IIII.}}</noinclude>roote in them selues, but are temporal: aftervvard vvhen tribulation is risen and persecution for the vvord, forthvvith they are scandalized. {{verse|chapter=4|verse=18}}† And other there be that are sovven among thornes: these are they that heare the vvord, {{verse|chapter=4|verse=19}}† and the cares of the vvorld and the deceitfulnes of riches, and concupiscences about other things entring in choke the vvord, and it is made fruiteles. {{verse|chapter=4|verse=20}}† And these are they that vvere sovven vpon the good ground, vvhich heare the vvord and receiue it, and yeld fruite one thirtie, one sixtie, and one an hundred.

{{verse|chapter=4|verse=21}}† And he said to them, {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Lu. 8, 16.''}}* Commeth a candel to be put {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=∷ Christ came not to teach his doctrine in corners and hucker mucker, as Heretikes doe, but to lighten the whole world therewith.}}∷ vnder a bushel, or vnder a bed? and not to be put vpon the candlesticke? {{verse|chapter=4|verse=22}}† For there is nothing hid, vvhich shal not be made manifest: neither vvas any thing made secret, but that it shal come to light. {{verse|chapter=4|verse=23}}† If any man haue eares to heare, let him heare.

{{verse|chapter=4|verse=24}}† And he said to them, See vvhat you heare. {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Lu. 8, 18.''}}* In vvhat measure you mete, it shal be measured to you againe, and more shal be giuen {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''`to you that heare''.}}`to you'. {{verse|chapter=4|verse=25}}† For he that hath, to him shal be giuen: and he that hath not, that also vvhich he hath, shal be taken avvay from him.

{{verse|chapter=4|verse=26}}† And he said, So is the kingdom of God, as if a man cast seede into the earth, {{verse|chapter=4|verse=27}}† {{sup|‖}} and sleepe, and rise vp night and day, and the seede spring, and grovve vp vvhiles he knovveth not. {{verse|chapter=4|verse=28}}† For the earth of it self bringeth forth fruite, first the blade, then the eare, aftervvard the ful corne in the eare. {{verse|chapter=4|verse=29}}† And vvhen the fruite hath brought out it self, immediatly he putteth in the sickle, because haruest is come.

{{verse|chapter=4|verse=30}}† {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Mat. 13, 31. Luc. 13, 19.''}}* And he said, To vvhat shal vve liken the kingdom of God? or to vvhat parable shal vve compare it? {{verse|chapter=4|verse=31}}† As a {{sup|‖}} mustard seede: vvhich vvhen it is sovven in the earth, is lesse then al the seedes that are in the earth: {{verse|chapter=4|verse=32}}† and vvhen it is sovven, it riseth vp, and becommeth greater then al herbes, and maketh great boughes, so that the {{sup|‖}} birdes of the aire may dvvel vnder the shadovv thereof.

{{verse|chapter=4|verse=33}}† And vvith many such parables he spake to them the vvord, according as they vvere able to heare: {{verse|chapter=4|verse=34}}† and vvithout parable he did not speake vnto them. but apart, he explicated al things to his Disciples.

{{verse|chapter=4|verse=35}}† And he saith to them in that day, vvhen euening vvas come, {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Mt. 8, 23. Lu. 8, 22.''}}* Let vs passe ouer to the other side. {{verse|chapter=4|verse=36}}† And dimissing the multitude, they take him so as he vvas in the boate: and there<noinclude>{{rh|||vvere}}</noinclude>
